#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Downloads the JSON Swagger document
cd `dirname $0`
set -e
stage=dev
region=us-east-1 # must match serverless.yml:provider.region
apiId=`bash -c "aws apigateway get-rest-apis --output=json --region=$region | /usr/bin/env node ./extract-rest-api-id.js $stage"`
fileType=json
outputFileName=serverless-aws-documentation-example-$STAGE.$fileType
printf "Downloading Swagger definition to ./$outputFileName
  API ID: $apiId
   Stage: $stage
  Accept: $fileType\n\n"

aws apigateway get-export \
  --rest-api-id=$apiId \
  --stage-name=$stage \
  --export-type=swagger \
  --accept=application/$fileType \
  --region=$region \
  $outputFileName

printf "\n$(tput setaf 2)Done, your swagger document is: ./$outputFileName$(tput sgr0)\nGo to http://editor.swagger.io/ and paste the contents of your swagger document to see it in Swagger UI"

This behavior facilitates automated retrieval and local storage of API definitions, which could be leveraged for reconnaissance or further automated attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated searching, archiving, and exfiltration of user files during installation is a hallmark of info-stealing malware, especially when performed without user consent and using hardcoded network destinations.

malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Backup utilities or deployment tools may archive and upload files, but only with explicit user consent, configuration, and secure authentication—not with hardcoded credentials or during package installation.
